liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, taking cash liquidity to revenue down by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, still above the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2025}}.
That cash pile covers the whole debt stock of {{total_debt@FY2025}} many times over, so near-term maturities are met from existing cash without new funding.
Free cash flow after lease payments fell by {{fcf_after_leases.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_after_leases@FY2025}}, as net capex rose by {{net_capex.change@FY2025}} to {{net_capex@FY2025}}.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow after lease payments fell by {{fcf_after_leases.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_after_leases@FY2025}} as net capex rose by {{net_capex.change@FY2025}} to {{net_capex@FY2025}}, so the investment programme now absorbs most of the cash the group generates.

Cash liquidity: cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, and cash liquidity to revenue declined by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, a thinner buffer against the capital spending plan.

Investment: capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2025}}, which keeps pressure on free cash flow while the programme runs.

Cost base: personnel expenses rose on collective wage increases and additions to personnel provisions, partly related to underutilisation, and the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}.
